Beállítom Az Egyesült Államok elnökét egy élelmiszer-szállító teherautó rakterében csempészik le az elnöki különgépről, hogy aztán mindenki elől elrejtve átszállhasson egy másik, kisebb repülőgépre. Az pedig végül titokban a valódi Air Force One-ként repül a megszokott gép után. Ilyen forgatókönyvet leginkább filmekben lehet látni, az amerikai sajtóban megjelent beszámolók szerint azonban pontosan ez történt, amikor Donald Trump július 8-án hazaindult Ankarából, a NATO-csúcstalálkozó után. Az amerikai elnököket védő Secret Service az elmúlt évtizedekben többször is használt csaligépeket és páncélautókat, ha a fenyegetés szintje azt megkövetelte. A legismertebb eset 2000-ben történt, amikor Bill Clinton akkori amerikai elnök Pakisztánba repült, és az amerikai hírszerzés attól tartott, hogy Oszama bin Laden terrorszervezete, az al-Kaida merényletet kísérelhet meg ellene. A beszámolókban megjelent taktikához hasonló manőver Trumpnak sem volt újdonság, miután a 2024-es elnökválasztás alatt kampánystábja tett már hasonló lépéseket iráni fenyegetések miatt. Úgy tudni, most is iráni merényletveszély miatt volt szükség a fokozott biztonsági intézkedésekre. Az ankarai esetről több lapnak is beszámoltak források, a Fehér Ház pedig nem cáfolta, hogy megtörtént. A CBS szerint viszont a Trump-kormány több tisztviselője is kifogásolta, hogy szigorúan titkos taktikák és módszerek szivárogtak ki a nyilvánosságba, ami a jövőben nehezebbé teheti az amerikai elnökök védelmét. Ételszállító teherautóban vihették át a gépek között Trump július 6-án érkezett meg Ankarába, a NATO-csúcsra, ahova Air Force One-ként az új, Katartól kapott gépet használva utazott. Amikor két nappal később hazaindult, már nem az új gépbe szállt be, hanem a régibe, amelyet korábban rendszeresen kritizált. Az erről készült felvételen látni lehetett, ahogy az elnök a New York Times akkori beszámolója szerint szokatlanul gyorsan felment a géphez tolt lépcsőn, integetett, majd beszállt a gépbe. Nagyjából öt perccel később egy, a másik oldalon álló catering teherautó elindult a géptől. Az élelmiszer-szállításra használt, megemelhető rakterű teherautóban ekkor már ott volt az Egyesült Államok elnöke is – írta meg először a Washington Post, aminek értesüléseit először a New York Times , majd később a CBS News és a CNN is megerősítette, névtelenül nyilatkozó amerikai tisztviselőkre hivatkozva. A teherautó, amibe Trump állítólag több munkatársával együtt szállt be, a gépnek a sajtó munkatársai és a kamerák által nem látható oldalán volt. A Post cikke szerint a teherautóval egy másik amerikai kormányzati géphez vitték az elnököt. Ott megemelték a rakodóteret, így jutott be Trump titokban a másik repülőgépbe, amelybe Pete Hegseth amerikai védelmi miniszter a rendes lépcsőn át szállt be. A gépet, egy C–32A típusú, átalakított Boeing 757-est magas rangú kormányzati tisztviselők utazására szokták használni. Az általában az elnök különgépeként használt eredeti repülő megtévesztésként az Air Force One hívójelet használva Nagy-Britanniába repült, a fedélzetén az elnök útjáról tudósító újságírókkal és Trump több munkatársával együtt, akik mind azt hitték, hogy az elnök is velük utazik. Mivel az Air Force One valójában annak a gépnek a hívójele lenne, amin ténylegesen az elnök tartózkodik, ebben az esetben titokban a C–32A töltötte be ezt a funkciót. A Mildenhall légibázisnál elsőként az új, Katartól kapott gép szállt le, majd az ott videózó planespotterek felvételei szerint nagyjából négy órával később az elnököt titokban szállító C–32A, pár perccel később pedig az Air Force One-nak hitt csaligép. Azt nem lehet tudni, hogy Trumpot hogyan sikerült titokban visszacsempészni ez utóbbi gépre, ami körül a CNN szerint a szokásosnál nagyobb biztonsági készültség volt. Trump végül erről szállt az új, Katartól kapott elnöki gépre, és azzal repült vissza az Egyesült Államokba. Ételszállító teherautó a régi Air Force One-ként használt Boeing mellett, indulás előtt az ankarai Esenboğa repülőtéren, 2026. július 8-án – Fotó: Saul Loeb / AFP A régi gép jobb? Az akkori beszámolók mind arról szóltak, hogy Trump a régi különgépén repült el Ankarából. Az elnök erre akkor azt a magyarázatot adta, hogy „a régi idők kedvéért” repül a megszokott géppel, valamint azért, hogy az új gépet meg tudják nézni a Mildenhall légibázison szolgáló katonák. A New York Times, majd a CBS News azonban azt írta, hogy biztonsági okokból, a Secret Service kérésére használták a régi gépet, mert a Katartól kapott és az elnöki használatra sietve átalakított új gépnek nem voltak még megfelelő védelmi eszközei. Július végén pedig már a CBS és a Times is arról számolt be, hogy valósnak ítélt iráni fenyegetések álltak a gépcsere hátterében. Mindkét médium értesülései szerint a Katartól kapott és nagyjából négyszázmillió dolláros költséggel átalakított új gépen nincsenek olyan fejlett rakétaelhárító rendszerek, mint a régi repülőn, és az amerikai légierő lapnak nyilatkozó egykori tisztviselői meglepőnek nevezték, hogy Trump azt külföldi utazásra használta. Ráadásul az iráni háború alatt az Iránnal szomszédos Törökországba, amit korábban az iráni rezsim elvétve rakétákkal támadott. Szakértők a Timesnak azt mondták, hogy két évbe is beletelik egy új gép felkészítése az elnöki használatra, és akár egymilliárd dollárt is felemészthet. A Trump-kormány nyomozást indított a géppel kapcsolatos kiszivárogtatások miatt, és idézéseket nyújtottak be a Times több újságírójával szemben. Híváslistákat akartak tőlük megszerezni, de később visszavonták a kereseteket, miután a bíróság megkérdőjelezte azok törvényességét. A Fehér Ház kommunikációs igazgatója, Steven Cheung akkor közleményben védte meg az új gépet: szerinte csúcstechnológiás és magas szintű biztonsági funkciói vannak. Ahogyan azt az elnök nemrégiben kijelentette, számos olyan ellensége van Amerikának, amelyek őt vették célba; „mi pedig minden rendelkezésünkre álló eszközt – beleértve a figyelemelterelést és a megtévesztést is – felhasználunk e fenyegetések kezelésére” – mondta. A katari gépet ezután azért továbbfejlesztették . Az akkori közlemény most újra a figyelem középpontjába került a figyelemelterelés és megtévesztés szavak használata miatt. A legújabb hírekre reagálva, miszerint Trumpot ételszállító teherautóval csempészték át egy másik gépre, a Fehér Ház szó szerint Cheung korábbi közleményét adta ki újra, az egyetlen különbség az volt, hogy a két szó hiányzott belőle. Az amerikai sajtóban megjelent beszámolók szerint egy Iránnal kapcsolatba hozható valós fenyegetés hatására reptették ki mindenki elől rejtve Trumpot Ankarából. A Times értesülései szerint pár óra alatt dolgozták ki a tervet, miután tisztviselők valósnak ítélték a fenyegetést, ami nem a katari gép ellen irányult, hanem bármilyen repülő ellen, ami az elnököt szállítja. A megtévesztési tervről csak pár kormányzati tisztviselő tudott, köztük Dan Caine tábornok, a vezérkari főnökök egyesített tanácsának elnöke, valamint Pete Hegseth. Trump az első elnöksége óta iráni célpontnak számít, miután elrendelte az iráni Forradalmi Gárda akkori nagy hatalmú vezetője, Kászim Szulejmáni ellen Irakban végrehajtott légicsapást. A 2024-es elnökválasztás alatt Trump már használt csaligépeket, miután arról számoltak be tisztviselők a kampánystábjának, hogy iráni ügynökök törnek az életére, és föld-levegő rakétákhoz is hozzáférnek. Alex Isenstadt amerikai újságíró könyve szerint Trump titokban Steve Witkoff amerikai üzletember, jelenlegi különleges követ magángépével repült, amit „szellemjáratként” emlegettek, miközben a stábja Trump magángépét használta. A Katartól kapott új VC–25B „Bridge” repülőgép landol az Ankarához közeli Etimesgut légibázison, a 36. NATO állam- és kormányfői csúcstalálkozó előtt, 2026. július 7-én – Fotó: Abdullah Güçlü / POOL / AFP Csaliautó, csalihelikopter, csalirepülő A Secret Service korábban rendszeresen használt csaliautókat és -repülőket arra, hogy titokban szállítsanak elnököket – mondta a New York Timesnak Donald Mihalek, a Secret Service egykori ügynöke, aki Barack Obama és George W. Bush biztonsági csapatának is tagja volt. „Valahányszor az elnök olyan hadszíntéren tartózkodik, ahol fennáll a harc veszélye, a Secret Service védelmi ellenintézkedéseket alkalmaz, köztük a csalik használatát is” – mondta Mihalek. Megvédte a titkolózást, mint mondta, ilyen esetben az elnök biztonsága fontosabb, mint az átláthatóság. Hasonlóan fogalmazott a Washington Postnak Ronald L. Rowe Jr., a Secret Service egykori ideiglenes vezetője, aki közölte, hogy „a nyilvánosságnak tudnia kell, mit tesz az elnök a mindennapokban, de ami azokat a módszereket illeti, amelyekkel a szolgálat az elnök biztonságát szavatolja, nos, azoknak rejtve kell maradniuk”. A lapnak egy amerikai kormányzati tisztviselő azt mondta, hogy az elmúlt harminc évben már többször is előfordult, hogy a máskor az elnök utazásaihoz használt, megszokott repülőt csaligépként vetették be súlyos fenyegetések miatt, vagy amikor veszélyes helyszínre utaztak. Ez azért van, mert az elnöki különgép nagyon biztonságos, de egyben nagyon feltűnő is, és így mégis biztonságosabb az elnököt titokban szállítani egy másik gépen. A legismertebb ilyen eset az volt, amikor Clinton 2000-ben Indiából Pakisztánba utazott. Amikor Mumbaiban búcsút intett Indiának, úgy tűnt, hogy egy C–17-es teherszállító gépbe száll be, de végül két kisebb Grumman Gulfstream C–20 típusú gép felé vette az irányt a nagy repülőgép takarásában. Az egyik festése jelezte, hogy az egy hivatalos amerikai kormányzati gép, a másik azonban sima fehér-ezüst festésű volt. Az elnök végül ebben utazott Iszlámábádba, ahol először a másik, csalinak használt gép szállt le és gurult oda a Clintonra várakozó emberekhez. Abból először a Secret Service egyik, Clintonra hasonlító ügynöke szállt ki az akkori beszámolók szerint . A jelzés nélküli C–20-asok Garrett M. Graff amerikai történész és újságíró cikke szerint évtizedek óta követik az elnököket, létezésük nyílt titoknak számít. De nem csak gépekből vannak csalik, a Secret Service-nek több hasonló páncélautója is van, hogy ne lehessen mindig tudni, az elnök melyikben utazik. A „csaliautón” is ott vannak az amerikai zászlók, és az elnöki pecsét , sőt, még a rendszáma is ugyanaz : 800-002. Clintont 2000-ben a repülőtéren például hat ugyanolyan kinézetű limuzin várta, amelyek sorrendet cseréltek, miután elhagyták a repülőteret a város felé. Emellett az elnököket szállító Marine One hívójelű helikopter is több másikkal együtt szokott repülni, hogy megnehezítsék az esetleges támadók dolgát. Amikor pedig Trump a kongresszusba utazott évértékelő beszédére, biztonsági okokból több ugyanolyan konvoj indult el a Fehér Házból. Önkéntelen csalik Az ankarai utazásról szóló cikkek megemlítették, hogy a valójában Trump nélküli gépen utazó újságírók és fehér házi dolgozók mind csalik lettek, anélkül hogy erről tudtak volna. „A gépen mindenki csalétek volt. Ha úgy ítélték meg, hogy nem biztonságos a gépen tartózkodni, akkor az mindenki másra nézve is veszélyes volt. Így legalább annyit mindenképpen megérdemelnek, hogy megtudják – ha nem előtte, hát utólag –, miért is történt mindez” – mondta a CNN-nek David Axelrod, Barack Obama egykori politikai főtanácsadója. Amikor újságírók arról kérdezték Trumpot, hogy miért kellett lehúzniuk az ablakokon az elsötétítőket, az elnök közölte, hogy azért, mert „valószínűleg egy veszélyes repülőn vagytok a mocskok miatt”, akikkel tárgyalniuk kell, utalva az iráni vezetésre. „Én vagyok a listájuk elején, előttetek, de ha nekem végem, akkor nektek is, igaz?” Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! MARGARET BRENNAN: I'm Margaret Brennan in Washington.And this week on Face the Nation; Iran apparently blinks after threats from President Trump for a major joint U.S. and Israel attack on Iranian soil.Heading in to a sixth month of conflict with Iran, President Trump told reporters Friday he had plans to go full throttle on his threat for military action in Iran.(Begin VT)DONALD TRUMP (President of the United States): We will be hitting them. We will be hitting them very hard. At some point, they're going to say, we just can't take it anymore.(End VT)MARGARET BRENNAN: His vows for going big caused a flurry of diplomatic scrambling and yet another announcement of – quote – "perimeters of a deal." But is this the one that's for real? We will have the latest.Plus: After an alarming incident of OpenAI going rogue and hacking into at least one company's computer system, we will talk to the CEO of Hugging Face, Clement Delangue.Finally, with polls showing Americans souring on both political parties, we will talk with former Senator Joe Manchin about his latest effort to encourage independents to join the process.It's all just ahead on Face the Nation.Good morning, and welcome to Face the Nation.President Trump's threat to massively escalate attacks on Iran set off a diplomatic scramble on Saturday. American allies, including the Saudi crown prince, urged the president to back off plans to bomb Iran's energy infrastructure.Late last night, Trump said military action at levels unseen since World War II remained an option. But he's holding off for now, at the request of allies, as well as Iran, because, he claimed, there was a diplomatic opportunity or, as he put it – quote – "the perimeters of a deal" has been agreed to.This morning, diplomatic sources tell me that there is no deal yet, but, rather, signs of progress towards an arrangement with Iran to reopen the strait. The challenge remains just how much leverage Iran will maintain over it.We turn now to Arizona Democratic Senator Mark Kelly, who joins us from Columbus, Ohio, this morning.Good morning to you, Senator.SENATOR MARK KELLY (D-Arizona): Good morning, Margaret.MARGARET BRENNAN: We're now in the sixth month of this war we had been told would last four to five weeks. In the past week, the targets have widened. Iran hit Egypt. We saw Saudi Arabia join the U.S. in bombing Iranian-backed militias there.And then, late last night, President Trump used the term that he had been considering military action on levels unseen since World War II. You sit on Intelligence. You sit on Armed Services. Has the administration shared anything in regard to its plans on Iran?SENATOR MARK KELLY: I mean, not these latest plans.And I think what we're seeing here is a president who has an approach to this that's just rather erratic. He says one thing, he does another thing. It's escalatory at this point. He's trying to get us back to February. And I think, if he could, he would – if he had a big reset button he could hit, he would certainly take that option.Hey, we've got 18 dead Americans. Prices have skyrocketed across the country for the American people. I was here in Ohio. I'm here in Ohio now, but I met with some veterans the other day, and they're struggling. I mean, these are a lot of retired service members that can't afford to put gas in their car, can't afford groceries.Rent is going up. And this president is not dealing with the issues that the American people need him to deal with.MARGARET BRENNAN: Well, you know, in our polling, we see that this is a very unpopular war, and it's weighing on the president's own approval ratings.But Democrats are faring slightly worse, according to CBS polling. When asked who has the better approach to Iran, 32 percent say Trump and the GOP. Only 30 percent say the Democrats. So we are in this thing. Do Democrats need to offer an affirmative vision for ending it?SENATOR MARK KELLY: Well, I don't think it's the president's vision.Here's a guy who got us into this without a strategic goal, without a plan, without a timeline. He's got a secretary of defense that doesn't know how to manage this war, who decided a good metric at the beginning was just to drop as many munitions as he could on as many targets, and now we've got a munitions shortage. Big surprise.So they're flailing. They're stuck. They're responsible for this. And the president is the one that has to try to figure out a way out of this. I would suggest to him, though, that the solution is not to do the same thing that he's been doing, not to have his real estate buddy and his son-in-law in charge of a negotiation, to put some people in here that know how to do this, how to talk to the Iranians, and put a coalition together, bring our allies back together.He's alienated not only our GCC allies, but our European allies as well. And it's just making this much harder for him to figure out a way out.MARGARET BRENNAN: But "The Washington Post" is reporting that the top U.S. general in Europe, General Grynkewich, warned the Pentagon that he lacks resources to protect Israel from incoming ballistic missiles, and if he's without another Navy destroyer, he will be forced to choose between defense of the homeland versus that of Israel.It sounds like, for the moment, Israel's not rejoining combat operations. But what does that say to you? Have you heard these concerns from this top commander yourself?SENATOR MARK KELLY: I haven't heard this specifically from Grynkewich on - - on this issue.But we – it's – it's not – Margaret, it's not – this isn't rocket science. It's not hard to figure out. I mean, we – we struck over 14,000 targets with multiple munitions. That – that is – puts a lot of stress on the magazine depth.So, of course, our commanders, probably not only in Europe, but in other places, are starting to feel some stress on, can they meet the need if they need to defend the homeland or our allies? You can see why this is an issue for him.And that's because, at the beginning of this thing, there was no strategic goal. And, without the goal, it's hard to figure out what to do next.MARGARET BRENNAN: Yes.SENATOR MARK KELLY: And I think that's why – that – you know, that's why Hegseth went just to try to set records on the number of targets hit.MARGARET BRENNAN: Yes.I should say for the record that the Pentagon says it's media speculation, and they don't comment on operational capabilities. We did ask them to clarify that.But on the point about restocking, Secretary Hegseth says he needs money from Congress to do that, to replenish munitions. He needs money from Congress to pay salaries. He needs $67 billion. You recently were asked, and you said you were undecided on how you would vote on additional funding. How do you deny that needed funding?SENATOR MARK KELLY: Well, Margaret, last year, we passed a defense budget that was over a trillion dollars. That was the first time ever. It was sold to us as a one-time generational investment in the department.And, in my view, they squandered that. Now they're coming and they're asking for $1.5 trillion, plus a supplemental. We're going to – we're approaching the amount of money that every other country on the planet spends on defense in a year.This is irresponsible. And now they want a blank check. Hey, I'm going to make sure the troops have what they need to defend themselves and defend the United States.MARGARET BRENNAN: So you would vote for the 67?SENATOR MARK KELLY: But they need to come to us – no, not – no, not necessarily.They need to come to us with a reasonable approach here. The $1.5 trillion, you know that has systems that I am very confident aren't going to work. They're still working on space-based interceptors for ICBMs. The physics on this is really very, very challenging. It's not going to make us safer, the other systems that we don't need.They – they need to understand that we do not have unlimited resources in this country.MARGARET BRENNAN: Yes.SENATOR MARK KELLY: We've got $39.5 trillion in debt. And the defense budget that they're requesting is twice what it was…MARGARET BRENNAN: Yes.SENATOR MARK KELLY: … when I got to the United States Senate in 2021. It's twice that budget.MARGARET BRENNAN: Well, you mentioned that you're in Ohio right now, and you are campaigning for fellow Democrats there.We're about 90 days out from the midterms. We looked at some recent Quinnipiac polling. It showed Democrats have a 23 percent – 2-3 percent – approval rating, worse than President Trump's approval.You've got a lot of headwinds. Republicans have an advantage in terms of fund – over Democrats in terms of funding. There's redistricting that I know Democrats say disadvantages them, though they've also gerrymandered. We see interparty fighting in Minnesota and in Michigan with no real promise to unify Democrats over a – a common candidate here.How concerned are you that – that Democrats are going to lose this thing or – or end up with this very, very tight race?SENATOR MARK KELLY: Well, I think we have an opportunity here, despite the Republican gerrymandering that started in – in the state of Texas, to try to you know rig the – the deck, so to say here, and make it more challenging.That – that provides an advantage to them. But this president is historically unpopular for a midterm president, and he's not meeting the needs of the American people. You know, gas is up over $4 a gallon. Half of Americans are having a hard time affording food, rent. Homeownership is down. Rent is up.The American people are really struggling. So we have an opportunity to win back the House, and I am confident we will. On the Senate side, it's challenging. I'm not going to – I'm not going to paint this as a rosy picture. But we've got 90 days to go.We have opportunities in a lot of different places, more than we thought we had six months ago. And a year-and-a-half ago, I would say we had no opportunity to win back the Senate. But because of the horrible job that Donald Trump has done for the American people, I think we have a chance we could win back control of the Senate.And that's why I'm here supporting Sherrod Brown. Add The New York Post on Google Misogynistic influencer Andrew Tate has been indicted for having sex with a minor, trafficking and money laundering – and allegedly recruited a 15-year-old girl for sexual exploitation, Romanian prosecutors announced Friday. Tate, 39, was issued with the fresh charges while he and his brother Tristan Tate, 38, remain detained at the Federal Detention Center in Miami, Fla., as they fight extradition back to the UK for alleged offenses that took place between 2010 and 2017. Tristan Tate has been charged with complicity as part of the investigation spearheaded by Romania’s Directorate for Investigating Organized Crime and Terrorism. Andrew Tate allegedly recruited a girl, who was 15, and sexually exploited her in the UK and Romania between 2012 and December 2021, according to prosecutors . 3 Andrew Tate is seen smoking a cigar and counting his money at his home in Romania in an undated social media image. Andrew Tate He allowed the girl to fall in love but used coercion, emotional blackmail, as well as physical aggression to ensure compliance, it is alleged. Explore More Glam influencer dragged from home, executed in front of her dad in horrifying gang hit Tourist’s death probe reopened after she’s killed by statue thrown from balcony— as mom ‘still waiting for justice’ Shark kills swimmer in attack off beach as witnesses recall seeing ‘pool of blood’ Tate allegedly forced the girl to produce sexually explicit material and practice so-called video chat activities for his pleasure, prosecutors alleged. While the alleged sexual exploitation occurred, Tristan Tate allegedly supported his brother rather than reporting the crime. Tristan Tate managed the girl’s video chat accounts and monitored her activity, prosecutors said. He also “resorted to acts of physical aggression [against the girl],” prosecutors said. The pair raked in more than $1.25 million from their alleged criminal activity. Andrew Tate also allegedly had sex with another 15-year-old child at two Romanian properties between December 2020 and mid-2021. 3 Andrew Tate and Tristan Tate are escorted by police officers outside the headquarters of the Directorate for Investigating Organized Crime and Terrorism (DIICOT) in Bucharest, Romania, on Dec. 29, 2022. REUTERS The brothers used money from sexual exploitation to splash out on four cars between December 2023 and July 2024, which had a combined value of $1.25 million. Investigators want to confiscate the cars. The Tate brothers had been living in Romania since 2016, where they are facing an investigation over allegations of human trafficking, rape, forming an organized criminal group, and money laundering. The brothers “continue to reject the allegations against them,” according to their attorney Eugen Constantin Vidineac. “Today’s decision by DIICOT does not determine guilt and it should not be presented as though it does. It represents the prosecution’s latest attempt to bring this case before a court following the failure of its previous indictment to proceed to trial,” he said. “The history of these proceedings matters. The previous indictment was subjected to judicial scrutiny and the court identified significant irregularities which prevented the case from moving forward to trial. “DIICOT has now chosen to file a new indictment. We will examine every aspect of it with the same level of scrutiny and we will challenge any evidential, procedural or legal deficiencies through the appropriate judicial process.” 3 Andrew and Tristan Tate sit as their lawyer urges a judge to release the brothers on bail as they contest extradition to Britain in this courtroom sketch on August 27, 2026 in Miami, Florida. via REUTERS Prosecutors announced the charges just three days after Vidineac warned to expect a new indictment, Forbes reported. He has called for the brothers to be released on bail amid fears that being incarcerated would result in them being found guilty in Romania. “I cannot guarantee the result of any proceeding or state that detention would inevitably cause the Tate brothers to lose in Romania,” he wrote in a Florida court filing. “But based on my direct experience representing them, if detention continues to deprive them of sustained, confidential, evidence-capable access to me during these critical stages, their ability to prepare and participate meaningfully—and, consequently, the defense’s prospects of obtaining favorable rulings—would be reduced to close to nil.” The Tates echoed their lawyer’s fears as they testified in a Miami courtroom last Thursday while shackled — a month after being arrested by US Marshals . Andrew Tate fears he will be slapped with an unfair life sentence in Eastern Europe while jailed on American soil. And Tristan Tate claimed he’s unable to prove his innocence while incarcerated. “I need to clear my name,” he said. “I need to take part in these proceedings, I can’t do that from the secure housing unit.” The Tate brothers face a combined 59 charges in the UK. Andrew Tate faces 42 charges for offenses involving seven victims. His charges include rape, controlling prostitution and arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation. In July, Andrew Tate was slapped with 19 extra charges for offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. Photograph: Christopher Oquendo/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen The ‘Goliath’ rollercoaster at Six Flags Over Georgia. Photograph: Christopher Oquendo/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock Georgia Man who died in Six Flags rollercoaster fall in Georgia was a father and educator Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem was a father of 10-year-old daughter, and overcame two bouts of cancer, his family says Keely Aouga Tue 13 Oct 2026 18.46 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Police on Tuesday identified the victim of the fatal accident at Six Flags Over Georgia as 42-year-old Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem of Atlanta. Kariem fell to his death after being ejected from his seat and several others were injured in an incident involving a rollercoaster at the theme park. Although authorities and Six Flags did not identify the rollercoaster, video footage shows passengers being evacuated from the park’s Goliath coaster. Kariem was a father to a 10-year-old daughter and an educator in Atlanta , Georgia. According to Atlanta public schools, Kariem started his career at Wesley International Academy as a technology teacher before being promoted to an IT Manager. “Atlanta Public Schools extends its deepest condolences to the family, friends, and loved ones of Mr Kariem,” a spokesperson for APS shared in a statement obtained by the Guardian. “He was a cherished member of the Wesley International Academy and APS families whose presence and impact will be deeply missed by our students, staff, and all those whose lives he touched,” the statement added. Wesley International Academy did not immediately return the Guardian’s request for comment. Kariem’s family spoke with 11Alive’s Chase Houle , and shared that he overcame many challenges in life, including two bouts of cancer. The last stint was in 2018. Additionally, his family said Kariem and his daughter survived a car fire three weeks ago. The two were unharmed in the incident. Cobb county police department’s major crimes unit has launched an investigation into Kariem’s death. It was unknown what led to the fatal accident, nor how the others were injured or their conditions. Since Kariem’s death, Six Flags temporarily closed nine rollercoasters across six amusement parks around the US. The incident comes less than two weeks after Six Flags Magic Mountain in southern California announced the permanent closure of its famous X2 rollercoaster amid lawsuits alleging serious brain injuries caused by the ride. The park had settled one wrongful death lawsuit from the family of a 22-year-old man who died after riding the coaster in 2022. Last year, a 32-year-old man died after riding a high-speed rollercoaster at the Universal Epic Universe theme park in Florida. He died from blunt impact injuries and his death was ruled accidental. According to a local Atlanta news station, Six Flags Over Georgia remains closed because of the offseason schedule and was expected to reopen on Friday. Coțofenești gold helmet (Photo: Muzeul Național de Istorie a României) Ion Puican , 25.10.2026, 14:00 The Coțofenești helmet is one of the most valuable gold artifacts ever discovered on the territory of Romania, belonging to the Thraco-Getic civilization. It was found by chance around 1927–1928 by a child from the village of Coțofenești, in the commune of Vărbilău, Prahova County, in the southern part of the country. The boy, who was out grazing sheep, wore the helmet on his head for several weeks. The piece was subsequently sold and ended up in the hands of a local merchant. In April 1929, it was purchased by the Romanian state and entered the National Museum of Antiquities’ collection; it later became part of the collection of the National History Museum of Romania (MNIR) in Bucharest, where it remains to this day. Museum curator Maria-Magdalena Ștefan, from the MNIR, tells us the story of this famous helmet: “The most significant discoveries about the world belong to children, and this is not merely a metaphor for the inquisitive spirit that defines humanity; it is also a literal truth, at least within the context of archaeology in Romania. The most famous cultural artifact in Romania today, the golden helmet from Coțofenești, as well as its counterpart from Cucuteni-Bădiceni, were discovered by children. We owe the 1928 discovery of the golden helmet, found on a wooded hillside in the Subcarpathian region, to a primary school boy, Traian Alexandru Simion, from the village of Coțofenești in Prahova County. We are located here not far from Vălenii de Munte, a site that once marked the beginning of a major transit route across the Carpathians. It is, therefore, no coincidence that such wealth was concentrated here, even if the area now appears wild and isolated. In those years, when the helmet first became known to the researchers of the time, most notably to university professor Ioan Andriescu, who conducted excavations at the discovery site in 1929, the Romanian public was still suffering from the loss of the “The Hatching Hen with Golden Chicks” (the Pietroasele treasure). At that time, the treasure had not yet returned from Russia, where it had been sent for safekeeping at the outbreak of the First World War; it seemed lost forever. Thus, the public life of the Coțofenești helmet began under the shadow of a collective sense of injustice and loss. From the very start, it was perceived as a symbolic form of restitution for what had previously been considered Romania’s most significant historical treasure. In the 98 years since its discovery, it has not only endured but has further solidified its status as a national symbol: it has appeared in the history textbooks used by generations of schoolchildren, and its image has even enjoyed a ‘cinematic career’”. The helmet dates back to the 4 th century BC and is crafted from high-purity gold, weighing 770 grams. Its surface features ritual scenes, large protective eyes, and fantastic animals, motifs typical of Thracian art, yet showing Greek and Scythian influences. Maria-Magdalena Ștefan provides further details on how this gold object was crafted and describes its decorations: “The helmet is a product of the metalworking art characteristic of the Thracians living north of the Balkan Mountains. Given the metal used and its decoration, the object appears to have held symbolic value. It was not merely a display of a military leader’s wealth; rather, it was almost certainly regarded as an object endowed with special powers, capable of bestowing certain attributes upon its wearer. The helmet weighs 770 grams and is nearly complete, only the apex of the skullcap is missing, having apparently broken off at some point between its discovery and its arrival at the museum. The alloy from which it is crafted contains approximately 20% silver, along with some copper and iron, a composition that refutes the hypothesis that it was made from native gold collected from rivers. Its open-faced design, characterized by straight lines, an elongated skullcap, and wide ear cutouts, allows us to identify its source of inspiration with considerable precision: it is a gold imitation of a bronze combat helmet. Specifically, it draws from the “Chalcidian” helmet style, produced in Greece and Southern Italy and highly prized by elite Thracian warriors, particularly during the 4 th century BC. The decoration on the skullcap, consisting of rosettes created by repoussé (pressed from the inside), resembles the ornamental motifs found on pieces of military equipment (such as neck and chest guards) used by the ancient Macedonians and the Balkan Thracians during the second half of the 4 th century BC. The specimen from Coțofenești is identical with the one used on the pectoral discovered in a famous tomb, perhaps the most famous in northern Greece, attributed to none other than Philip II, the father of Alexander the Great. Both the shape of the helmet (derived from Chalcidian types) and the decorative details, as well as the metal chosen, gold, point to a date for the helmet toward the end of the 4 th century BC. In short, it is approximately 2,300 years old. During this period, the communities in the regions surrounding the Aegean and Black Seas were reconfiguring their aristocratic beliefs and ideologies, and even their religious tenets, under the profound influence of the expansion of the Macedonian kingdoms under Philip II and Alexander the Great. This era marks the heyday of the Getae civilization. The most interesting decorative elements of the helmet are found on the cheek pieces and the neck guard. The cheek pieces feature a symmetrical, dual depiction of a sacrificial scene, one imbued with palpable drama, despite the naive, slightly clumsy artistic style: a warrior, armed with a dagger, pins a ram to the ground with all his might, pulling its muzzle upward to expose its throat. He is shown with his dagger raised, his cloak billowing in the wind, moments away from the kill. The sacrifice of an animal has always been the essential link between humanity and the divine; in the context of classical civilizations, rams were specifically regarded as creatures that ensured the link to the afterlife. On the neck guard, we can identify sphinxes and griffins, supernatural beings of Greek inspiration that serve as guardians of tombs and denizens of the fantastical realms at the fringes of the known world, symbolizing both transgression and religious experience. On the front of the helmet, wide-open eyes with prominent brows are depicted, surmounted by horns. In that era, horns were a sign of divinity, as we know from depictions of Alexander the Great.” In January 2025, the helmet, along with several Dacian gold bracelets, was stolen from the Drents Museum in Assen, the Netherlands, where it was on display as part of the international exhibition “Dacia! Kingdom of Gold and Silver.” The robbery was violent; the thieves used explosives to break into the museum, and the helmet sustained visible damage, its cheek guard was bent inward. Following an international investigation, the helmet was recovered in early April 2026, along with two of the three stolen bracelets. The search for the third bracelet continues. The gold artifacts have been returned to Romania and handed over to the National History Museum, where the helmet is currently undergoing restoration under the supervision of the National Commission for Museums and Collections. Experts estimate that restoring it to its original form will take approximately one year, unlike the bracelets, which were recovered intact.
